name: Coffeehouse2Home Property Ledger
brief: Coffeehouse2Home is one software suite for a property-services company that does brokerage, house flipping, rentals, and field services, run by one shared Property Ledger: every property has a single record (ownership, address, status, full history) shared across all five domains. The real-estate CRM tracks contacts, buyer and seller leads, and a deal pipeline with stages; any listing, flip, or rental property can publish showing slots (private showings and open houses) that buyers book with email confirmation, reminders, calendar-sync stub, and a per-property showing history with buyer feedback. The flip manager tracks acquisitions, renovation budgets with line items, contractor bids, flip project phases, and job costing per property. The rental portfolio manages leases, tenants, rent roll with payment records, maintenance requests, vacancy tracking, and lease-renewal reminders. The field-ops suite turns work orders raised from any property (a flip task, a maintenance request, a buyer-requested repair) into crew task lists, rolls crew time sheets into weekly payroll with rates and overtime, and tracks material/supply lists with purchase records and reorder flags. Cross-domain data flows: work-order hours feed payroll and job cost, showings on flip or rental properties create CRM buyer leads, and every property's deals, flips, leases, and work orders accumulate on its shared ledger record.

## Mission
Coffeehouse2Home is one software suite for a property-services company that does brokerage, house flipping, rentals, and field services, run by one shared Property Ledger: every property has a single record (ownership, address, status, full history) shared across all five domains. The real-estate CRM tracks contacts, buyer and seller leads, and a deal pipeline with stages; any listing, flip, or rental property can publish showing slots (private showings and open houses) that buyers book with email confirmation, reminders, calendar-sync stub, and a per-property showing history with buyer feedback. The flip manager tracks acquisitions, renovation budgets with line items, contractor bids, flip project phases, and job costing per property. The rental portfolio manages leases, tenants, rent roll with payment records, maintenance requests, vacancy tracking, and lease-renewal reminders. The field-ops suite turns work orders raised from any property (a flip task, a maintenance request, a buyer-requested repair) into crew task lists, rolls crew time sheets into weekly payroll with rates and overtime, and tracks material/supply lists with purchase records and reorder flags. Cross-domain data flows: work-order hours feed payroll and job cost, showings on flip or rental properties create CRM buyer leads, and every property's deals, flips, leases, and work orders accumulate on its shared ledger record.

## Mission
Coffeehouse2Home is one software suite for a property-services company that does brokerage, house flipping, rentals, and field services, run by one shared Property Ledger: every property has a single record (ownership, address, status, full history) shared across all five domains. The real-estate CRM tracks contacts, buyer and seller leads, and a deal pipeline with stages; any listing, flip, or rental property can publish showing slots (private showings and open houses) that buyers book with email confirmation, reminders, calendar-sync stub, and a per-property showing history with buyer feedback. The flip manager tracks acquisitions, renovation budgets with line items, contractor bids, flip project phases, and job costing per property. The rental portfolio manages leases, tenants, rent roll with payment records, maintenance requests, vacancy tracking, and lease-renewal reminders. The field-ops suite turns work orders raised from any property (a flip task, a maintenance request, a buyer-requested repair) into crew task lists, rolls crew time sheets into weekly payroll with rates and overtime, and tracks material/supply lists with purchase records and reorder flags. Cross-domain data flows: work-order hours feed payroll and job cost, showings on flip or rental properties create CRM buyer leads, and every property's deals, flips, leases, and work orders accumulate on its shared ledger record.

requirements: The system MUST maintain a single shared Property Ledger per property, where the record aggregates ownership, address, status, and full history, and where all updates from brokerage, flipping, rentals, or field services update that same record and its history.
The real-estate CRM MUST track contacts, buyer leads, seller leads, and a deal pipeline with configurable stages; each deal MUST be linkable to a property in the Property Ledger.
The system MUST allow any listing, flip, or rental property to publish showing slots, including private showings and open houses, each with a date/time and location reference.
Buyers MUST be able to book a showing slot by providing their email address; the system MUST send an email confirmation for each booking.
The system MUST send a reminder for each upcoming booked showing at a configured interval before the start time.

The system MUST provide a calendar-sync stub for each showing booking that outputs an ICS-compatible representation of the event (or a clearly marked placeholder), without requiring an external calendar provider.
Each property MUST maintain a per-property showing history that records every showing occurrence, the associated buyer, and any feedback the buyer provides after the showing.
The flip manager MUST track property acquisitions, renovation budgets with line items, contractor bids, flip project phases, and job costing per property, all linked to the Property Ledger.

The rental portfolio MUST manage leases, tenants, rent roll with payment records, maintenance requests, vacancy tracking, and lease-renewal reminders; each lease and tenant MUST be linked to a property in the Property Ledger.

The field-ops suite MUST accept work orders raised from any property context (flip task, maintenance request, buyer-requested repair) and convert them into crew task lists with assignments and status.
The field-ops suite MUST roll crew time sheets into weekly payroll calculations using recorded rates and overtime rules, and MUST feed work-order hours into both payroll and job cost.
The field-ops suite MUST track material and supply lists with purchase records and reorder flags.
When a showing occurs on a flip or rental property, the system MUST automatically create a CRM buyer lead for the buyer who attended, linked to the property and the showing history.

The Property Ledger for each property MUST accumulate and display cross-domain records including deals, flips, leases, work orders, showings, and any related history entries, so that any user in any domain can see the full property history.
edgeCases: A booking for a showing slot that has already passed or has zero remaining capacity MUST be rejected with an explicit error and MUST NOT create a lead or send a confirmation.
Two buyers attempting to book the same last available slot concurrently MUST result in exactly one successful booking and exactly one rejection (no double-book or lost update).
A showing slot that is published on a flip or rental property but has no attendees MUST still appear in the showing history with a status of 'no-show' or equivalent after its end time.
Duplicate email addresses in buyer leads (same buyer booking multiple showings) MUST NOT create duplicate CRM contacts; the same contact record MUST be reused and the new lead attached to it.
A work order that spans two payroll weeks MUST have its hours split across the weeks based on the time-sheet date so weekly payroll and job cost remain accurate.

Hourly rate or overtime multiplier must be applied correctly when a day's time-sheet totals exceed the daily overtime threshold; the overtime portion MUST be recorded separately in payroll and job cost.
Lease-renewal reminders MUST be generated for leases whose end date falls within a configurable look-ahead window; leases already renewed or terminated MUST NOT trigger reminders.
Vacancy tracking MUST reflect the transition when a lease ends and the property status is set to vacant, without duplicating vacancy records.
A material reorder flag MUST be set when the available quantity of a tracked supply falls below a defined threshold; adding inventory MUST clear the flag and record the purchase in purchase records.
If a property is deleted or deactivated, the system MUST NOT delete its ledger history or historical records; instead it MUST mark the property inactive while retaining all related records.
If the email delivery service is unavailable, the booking MUST be persisted and the confirmation/reminder status marked as 'pending', but the booking itself MUST NOT be lost.
Calendar-sync output for a showing MUST include a stable UID and be deterministic (same booking produces identical ICS content) to allow idempotent client syncs.
A buyer feedback submission for a showing that has no associated booking record MUST be rejected or logged with an error, and MUST NOT create a lead.

When a showing is published on a flip property that is not yet acquired, the property ledger status MUST reflect the intended use and the flip acquisition MUST update the status without losing the showing history.
errorHandling: Invalid input (e.g., malformed email, missing required fields such as property ID, showing time, or budget line amount) MUST be rejected with a validation error and no partial write occurs.

When a requested property ID does not exist in the Property Ledger, the operation (showing publish, booking, work order, lease creation, flip phase update) MUST fail with a clear not-found error and MUST NOT create a lead or record.
When the email service returns an error, the booking or reminder MUST be marked as 'email_failed' or equivalent, and the system MUST log the error with a retry flag but continue processing.

Concurrent updates to the same Property Ledger record (e.g., two domains writing to the same property) MUST be serialized or conflict-checked; on conflict, the later write MUST be rejected with a conflict error and the client must retry with the current state.
Payment record creation for rent MUST ensure the rent roll is updated atomically; a partial write (payment recorded but roll not updated) is forbidden and any such failure rolls back the transaction.
If the calendar-sync generation fails (e.g., invalid date), the system MUST return an error but the booking itself remains valid and the error is isolated to the stub generation.
If a weekly payroll calculation receives no time sheets for a week, it MUST produce a payroll record with zero hours and zero pay, not an exception, and the job cost MUST reflect zero.
If a work order references a nonexistent task or property, the system MUST reject the work order and MUST not allow crew time sheets to be attached.
When a buyer's email is duplicated during lead creation, the system MUST deduplicate by email and attach to the existing contact; no error is required, but duplicate records MUST NOT be created.
Lease-renewal reminder generation encountering a lease with invalid end date MUST log a warning and skip that lease, not fail the whole batch.

dataFlow: A property is created/imported into the Property Ledger, establishing a single record and empty history.

Any domain action (showing publish, booking, lease creation, flip phase, work order) is first validated against the property's existence and then written to the shared ledger record plus its domain table.

A showing booking starts with buyer email and slot; the system checks slot capacity/availability; after successful booking, it persists the booking and at the same time writes a showing history entry with status 'scheduled; it then queues and sends a confirmation email.
When a showing start time is within the reminder interval, the system generates and sends a reminder email for that booking; the ledger records the reminder activity.
When a buyer requests calendar sync, the system generates ICS content from the booking's date/time and stores/returns it; the ICS is deterministic.

After a showing ends, the system prompts the buyer for feedback; on feedback submission, it updates the showing history and pushes a buyer lead into the CRM (only for flip/rental properties) linked to the contact and property.
A CRM lead for a showing on flip/rental property is created using the buyer's email (deduplicated against existing contacts) and associated with the property ledger and the showing record.
A flip acquisition creates a flip project on the property; budget line items, contractor bids, and phase changes are each written to the flip domain and history ledger.
Rent payment is validated against an active lease, recorded in the rent roll, and a payment record is added to the property ledger history.
A maintenance request opens a work order in field ops, which is assigned to a crew; crew time is logged per work order and date.

Time entries are accumulated into task lists; at the end of a week, timesheets feed weekly payroll calculation (using rates and overtime rules) and simultaneously update the flip or rental job cost for each property.
Material supply usage reduces quantities; each purchase records the transaction and restores quantity; when quantity falls below threshold, a reorder flag is set and stored in the inventory record.
All ledger entries (deals, flips, leases, work orders, showings, payments, purchases) are appended to the property's ledger history for cross-domain visibility.
negativeConstraints: DO NOT create separate property records for different domains for the same physical property; every domain must reference the single shared Property Ledger record.
DO NOT drop or bypass the per-property showing history: every showing and feedback must be recorded on the property.
DO NOT allow a buyer to book a showing without a valid email or without reducing slot capacity atomically.
DO NOT create duplicate CRM contact records for the same email address.
DO NOT generate lease-renewal reminders for leases without an end date or for leases that are already renewed or terminated.
DO NOT delete a property's ledger history or related records when a property is inactivated.
DO NOT lose bookings or work orders if email delivery fails; persist them and mark email status as pending.
DO NOT split a single work order's time across multiple payroll weeks incorrectly: hours must be attributed to the actual week logged.
DO NOT perform payroll or job-cost calculations from unverified or partial time sheets; only approved time entries count.
DO NOT publish showing slots without a property reference that exists in the Property Ledger.
DO NOT allow a maintenance request or work order to reference a nonexistent property.
DO NOT include cross-domain data (such as CRM leads from showings) for properties that are not flip or rental properties.
DO NOT use generic 'property' entities across domains that do not share the same unified ledger record.
DO NOT implement external calendar providers such as Google Calendar; provide only a calendar-sync stub as described.
DO NOT generate a payroll record with negative hours or overtime rates that do not match configured rules; enforce non-negative and overtime-threshold logic.
DO NOT skip the reorder flag when material quantity drops below the defined threshold.
DO NOT store showing history or feedback without a property association.
DO NOT bypass the property's history ledger when writing deals, flips, leases, work orders, or payments.
